dashboard.label: SNMP — Splunk Connect (SC4SNMP)
dashboard.description: Real-time SNMP into Splunk via Splunk Connect for SNMP — polled metrics (GET) and pushed traps — from Proxmox and the Berlin services.

html.h2: SNMP via Splunk Connect for SNMP (SC4SNMP)
html.p: SNMP has two modes: GET/polling (the collector asks a device on UDP 161 every N seconds) and traps (the device pushes an alert to the collector on UDP 162 the moment something happens — the real-time bit). SC4SNMP (the supported Splunk tool) runs as a small Docker Compose stack on ubuntu-berlin-snmp (198.18.3.52) and ships both to Splunk over HEC.
Regional + RBAC: Berlin devices land in berlin_snmp (London in london_snmp when routers are added), so the same per-location wall applies — Ben sees Berlin SNMP, Leo London, Gary both.

search.query: | tstats count as c where index=berlin_snmp OR index=london_snmp | eval Status=if(c>0,"ACTIVE","NO DATA") | table Status c | rename c as Events
index=berlin_snmp OR index=london_snmp | stats dc(host) as hosts
index=berlin_snmp OR index=london_snmp | timechart span=1m count by sourcetype

index=berlin_snmp OR index=london_snmp | stats count as Events, latest(_time) as last by host sourcetype | eval "Last seen"=strftime(last,"%F %T") | rename host as Host, sourcetype as Sourcetype | table Host Sourcetype Events "Last seen" | sort - Events

ol.li: Collector: SC4SNMP (Docker Compose) on ubuntu-berlin-snmp — snmp/setup-sc4snmp.sh. It polls devices and listens for traps, then ships to Splunk HEC (enabled by apply.sh, index berlin_snmp).
Poll a device: enable its SNMP agent — e.g. Proxmox via snmp/enable-proxmox-snmpd.sh (community dcloud) — and add it to the SC4SNMP inventory.
Traps (real-time): point a device's trap sink at 198.18.3.52:162; the trap shows here within a second or two.

html.p: Runs independently of Proxmox (its own VM), so switching Proxmox off in a demo doesn't take the SNMP collector down with it.
